name: security-oauth-jarm-response-review
intent: JWT-secured authorization response trust and transaction binding
artifacts: JARM validation code, issuer/audience/algorithms, state/nonce lifecycle and callback/session consumer.
trace: Follow the signed authorization response through validation to code exchange and final session. Preserve the difference between authentic issuer data and correct client/transaction binding.
experiment: Use an owned client/issuer fixture and compare a valid response with a response for another owned client or expired transaction.
disproof: Correct JWT signature verification alone is not a full callback check; an error without a minted session rejects the attack hypothesis.
repair: Bind issuer, audience and transaction before exchange/session creation; retest valid, wrong-client and replay paths.
branch_decisions: Separate response signature/encryption processing from transaction state and authorization-code exchange. Verify issuer/audience and registered response mode/algorithms in context. A valid response for another owned client is a useful mismatch control; a malformed unsigned object rejected before parsing tests no transaction-binding property.
operational_method: Bind the verified response to one initiating browser transaction and consume its state according to the client replay policy. Keep code exchange tied to the expected issuer/client, redirect URI and PKCE transaction as applicable. Compare two concurrent transactions for the same client, not only different audiences. A valid signed response delivered to the wrong local transaction must not silently complete that other session.
